note: What WordPress offers today, with sources, for checking what agents claim. Kept by hand; re-check each month. confirmed=false means the source couldn't be fully verified.

facts.topic: Local setup with no database server
facts.fact: WordPress Playground CLI starts a local WordPress site with `npx @wp-playground/cli@latest start` (or `server`). It needs only Node.js 20.18+ and uses SQLite, so no MySQL server is required.

facts.topic: Local setup with no database server
facts.fact: The `start` command (announced 24 February 2026) keeps the site between sessions in ~/.wordpress-playground/sites/, with --blueprint, --php, --wp, --port, --login and --reset options.

facts.topic: Local setup with no database server
facts.fact: SQLite Database Integration is an official feature plugin (v3.0.2, 5,000+ installs), aimed at landing in core eventually. It suits development and low-traffic sites; SQLite allows one writer at a time.

facts.topic: Local setup with no database server
facts.fact: SQLite is not in WordPress core as of October 2026. The requirements page recommends PHP 8.3+ and MySQL 8.0+ or MariaDB 10.11+ for production.

facts.topic: Local setup with no database server
facts.fact: wp-env uses Docker by default, and has an experimental `wp-env start --runtime=playground` that runs WordPress on SQLite with no Docker.

facts.topic: Local setup with no database server
facts.fact: WordPress Studio is a free, open-source desktop app for local WordPress on macOS, Windows and Linux. It uses SQLite instead of a MySQL server.

facts.topic: Local setup with no database server
facts.fact: Studio has a CLI to create, start and stop local sites and create preview sites, and connects to Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code through MCP.
WordPress.com has a $0 Free plan with no expiry: hosting, automatic updates, unlimited pages and posts, 1 GB storage, on a wordpress.com subdomain, with ads and no plugins.
WordPress.com paid plans, billed yearly: Personal $4/month, Premium $8/month, Business $25/month, Commerce $45/month. All paid plans can install plugins.
Hostinger, one of three hosts recommended on wordpress.org, has WordPress plans reported from about $2.99/month on a long term, renewing around $10.99/month (third-party review).
wordpress.org recommends three hosts: Pressable, Bluehost and Hostinger.
Static hosting can be free: GitHub Pages (public repos, not for commercial or e-commerce use), Netlify's $0 plan, and Vercel's $0 Hobby plan for personal projects.
Since WordPress 3.7, minor and security core releases and translations install automatically by default.
Since WordPress 5.6, new installs auto-update to major core releases too, by default.
Since WordPress 5.5, admins can turn on auto-updates for plugins and themes; they run twice a day with email notices. They are opt-in, apart from critical security pushes.
WordPress 7.0.2 (17 July 2026) fixed a critical REST API SQL injection in core; WordPress.org forced the update through auto-updates and backported fixes.
WordPress.com includes automatic updates on every plan, including Free, so the host handles them.
Patchstack counted 11,334 new WordPress-ecosystem vulnerabilities in 2025: 91% in plugins, 9% in themes, and 6 in core, all low priority.
46% of 2025's WordPress vulnerabilities had no fix at disclosure; premium components had 3 times as many known exploited vulnerabilities as free ones.
Wordfence's 2024 report found 5 of that year's disclosed vulnerabilities affected core; plugins were 96% of vulnerable software.
The WordPress Security Team has more than 50 experts, backports fixes to older branches and pushes them through auto-updates.
Simply Static (free, 30,000+ installs) exports a WordPress site as static files to host on GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify or Vercel. Forms and search need Pro ($99/year).
A secondary source citing the HTTP Archive says 48.7% of WordPress origins passed Core Web Vitals on mobile in August 2026, against 53.0% of all origins, with slow TTFB the main gap.
WordPress 7.1 (19 August 2026) processes images in the browser, reducing server load and file sizes.
The block editor has been the default since WordPress 5.0 (December 2018), with drafts, previews and visual editing without code.
Core includes Administrator, Editor, Author, Contributor and Subscriber roles, so multi-author publishing with review needs no plugin.
WordPress 7.1 added Notes with @mentions for editorial feedback in the editor.
WooCommerce core has three shipping methods: Flat Rate, Free Shipping and Local Pickup.
Core WooCommerce has no weight-based rate calculation; Flat Rate formulas support quantity and percentage fees only.
Weight-based tiers come with WooCommerce's paid Table Rate Shipping extension (about USD $119/year, unconfirmed).
The free Weight Based Shipping for WooCommerce plugin (50,000+ installs, updated October 2026) supports weight-range tiers and rates by country.
WooCommerce core includes stock management: quantities, held stock, low and out-of-stock alerts, and backorders.
Paid Memberships Pro's core plugin is free and open source (levels, content restriction, checkout), downloaded from paidmembershipspro.com rather than wordpress.org.
LifterLMS core is free with no limits on courses, memberships or enrolments, and includes Stripe and PayPal payments.
Tutor LMS's free version (100,000+ installs) includes unlimited courses, quizzes, certificates and course selling with PayPal and Stripe.
Sensei LMS by Automattic is free for courses, lessons, quizzes and progress; selling courses and drip content need Sensei Pro.
LearnDash is paid only, from $259/year.
Core's Tools > Export produces a WXR file with posts, pages, comments, custom fields, taxonomies and users; the free WordPress Importer imports it.
`wp export` in WP-CLI writes WXR files, filtered by post type, date or author.
The core REST API (since WordPress 4.7) reads and writes content as JSON.
Markdown-in-Git workflows need plugins, such as Git it Write (publishes Markdown from a GitHub repo). Core has no Markdown export.
WordPress.com GitHub Deployments deploys theme and plugin code from GitHub, not content.

WordPress/agent-skills has 20 skills for AI coding assistants (blocks, block themes, plugins, REST API, WP-CLI, Playground, Blueprints, wp-env and more), installed with `npx skills add WordPress/agent-skills`. None helps an agent decide whether WordPress fits.
The Abilities API shipped in WordPress 6.9 (December 2025): a registry of site functions that PHP, REST and AI agents can call.
The WordPress MCP Adapter exposes Abilities to agents as MCP tools; it's a plugin or Composer package, not in core.
WordPress 7.0 (20 May 2026) added an AI Client and a Connectors hub for AI providers to core.

wordpress.org/llms.txt exists, with an 'AI and Agentic Development' section linking the REST API handbook and the MCP Adapter. It doesn't help an agent decide when WordPress fits, and states '43%+' share, above W3Techs' 40.1%.

facts.topic: Making an existing HTML site editable
facts.fact: Create Block Theme (official, 20,000+ installs) creates blank or child block themes, saves Site Editor changes to theme files and exports the theme.

facts.topic: Making an existing HTML site editable
facts.fact: No official tool or handbook page converts a static HTML site into a block theme automatically; it's rebuilt by hand.
W3Techs, 7 October 2026: WordPress runs 40.1% of all websites and 58.6% of sites with a known CMS.
